newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares shuffle sideways before long weekend.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares shuffle sideways before long weekend.

text.p: Italy's stock indices shuffled sideways in subdued trade on Thursday but held a positive tone ahead of a three-day holiday weekend despite a droop in futures at the finish.
The market is now closed until Monday. The blue-chip Mib30 index gained a mere 0.05 percent to 21,756 while the all-share Mibtel index was 0.05 percent stronger at 14,405.
But the Fib 30 September future fell 0.25 percent to 21935.
Brokers said activity was slack once volume related to options expiries at the opening had been discounted.
"It's a pre-holiday market without a precise direction," one broker said.
Blue-chips energy giant Eni and carmaker Fiat were both hit by sales and fell more than 1.4 percent each, with Eni 1.44 percent lower at 10075 and Fiat 1.8 percent off at 5620 lire.

Banca Commerciale Italiana (BCI) climbed more than two percent to 4550 lire after Italian brokers issued a positive rating with a target price of 5000 lire on expectations of a marked rise in profitability.
Dairy products group Parmalat was 1.74 percent higher at 2635 lire after a foreign broker's buy recommendation which forecast the price at 3,000 lire and beyond.
Telecom Italia remained stable, 0.43 percent down at 10945, unmoved by a study by investment house Morgan Stanley which gave it a target price of 13,000 lire.
